title: Knight steps
objective: Select a knight and move it in an L shape, then repeat without a source cue.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original beginner lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original practice position and teaching text; not a historical game

steps.explanation: Click the white knight, then click a square it can reach. Knights move two squares in one direction and one square to the side.
steps.detail: The white knight starts beside your king on g1. Try making an L shape.
steps.coach_prompt: First select your knight. Then choose its landing square.

question.prompt: Select the knight on g1, then move it to f3.
hints: Click the white horse-shaped piece beside your king.

tree.feedback: Yes. From g1 to f3 is an L shape: two squares up and one to the side.
That is a legal L-shaped jump. This time, try the other landing square: f3.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal, but this turn is for the knight. Return and try an L-shaped jump.

steps.explanation: The knight has moved. Find another L-shaped jump without a glowing starting square.
steps.detail: You can ask for a hint if you need one.
steps.coach_prompt: Find another knight jump on your own.

question.prompt: Choose another L-shaped jump for your knight.
hints: Find the knight in the middle of the board.

tree.feedback: Well done. From f3 to e5 is another L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to d2 is an L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to d4 is an L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to g1 is an L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to g5 is an L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to h2 is an L-shaped knight jump.
Yes. From f3 to h4 is an L-shaped knight jump.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move is legal. Return and try moving the knight in an L shape.

takeaway: A knight moves in an L: two squares one way and one square across.
